# `select_kernel_product`

the product of two or three stored kernel sets, mixed radix with the first factor fastest (the members a flow measurement is over).

Version 1, scope `subject`. Run it with `nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --dataset <folder> --subject <id> ...`; `nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --help` prints the same options.

Examples:

```
nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --first atoms --second bands --third bands --name "atoms x bands x bands"
```

## Inputs

| input | what it is | required |
|---|---|---|
| `first` | selection any, where {"name": "$first"} (the first kernel set (it varies fastest): e.g. the atoms (`nxr-neuro run select_kernels` first)) | yes |
| `second` | selection any, where {"name": "$second"} (the second kernel set: e.g. the eigenvalue bands) | yes |
| `third` | selection any, where {"name": "$third"}, when {"factors": 3} (the third kernel set (factors 3): e.g. the bands again, for band pairs) | yes |

## Parameters

Each is an option `--<name> VALUE` (dashes for underscores; the value is read as YAML) or `--set NAME=VALUE`.

| parameter | option | default | unit | choices | meaning |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `factors` | `--factors` | `2` | - | 2, 3 | how many kernel sets the product has: 2 (first, second) or 3 (first, second, third: e.g. atoms x bands x bands) |
| `first` | `--first` | `required` | - |  | the first kernel set's name (it varies fastest) |
| `second` | `--second` | `required` | - |  | the second kernel set's name |
| `third` | `--third` | none | - |  | the third kernel set's name (factors 3) |
| `name` | `--name` | `required` | - |  | the product's name |

## The chain of nodes

| phase | node | in | with | out |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | [`select.product`](../nodes.md) | first=first, second=second | layout=product | product_lines, product |
| before | [`select.product`](../nodes.md) | first=first, second=second, third=third | layout=product | product_lines_3, product_3 |

`before` steps run once, `chunks` steps run on every chunk of the recording, `after` steps run once on what the chunks accumulated.

## Outputs

| output | stored as |
|---|---|
| `product_lines` | kind manifold, type product, factors ["first.manifold.0", "second.manifold.0"], when {"factors": 2} |
| `product_lines_3` | kind manifold, type product, factors ["first.manifold.0", "second.manifold.0", "third.manifold.0"], when {"factors": 3} |
| `product` | kind selection, type product, name $name, on product_lines, factors ["first", "second"], when {"factors": 2} |
| `product_3` | kind selection, type product, name $name, on product_lines_3, factors ["first", "second", "third"], when {"factors": 3} |

## Notes from the definition

```text
THE PRODUCT OF KERNEL SETS: every combination of the members of two or three stored kernel sets (`select_kernels`), coded mixed radix with the FIRST
factor fastest (the node `select.product`, layout product). The flow pipelines measure over such products: the atoms x the eigenvalue bands (the
consistency per atom and band) and the atoms x the bands x the bands (the band pairs: the first factor the atom a, the second the band q at the tip, the third the band p at
the tail; code a + A (q + Q p)). A kernel set is a selection on its line (the frequency line, the eigenvalue line), so the product lies on the product of the lines.

  nxr-neuro run select_kernel_product --dataset <folder> --subject sub-01 --first atoms --second bands --third bands --name "atoms x bands x bands"
```
